item.title: Family trapped by powerful floodwaters until 2 neighbors grab a kayak and paddleboard
item.description: As rising floodwaters trapped a mother and a son in their home in Palm Bay, Florida, two neighborhood boys nearby used a kayak and a paddleboard to come to the rescue.
item.content:encoded:
After heavy rainfall caused severe flooding that trapped a desperate Florida family inside their home for hours, two neighborhood brothers with a paddleboard and kayak took dramatic action to do what they could to help. 

The rescue of a mother and son, plus their three dogs, took place Monday in Palm Bay, a city in Brevard County roughly 70 miles southeast of Orlando, as heavy rain flooded homes and streets across the area.

Brittany Grant, a Palm Bay resident, told ClickOrlando that floodwaters began pouring into her home — which forced her and her young son to climb onto the kitchen counter to dodge the rising water, she said.

ALLIGATOR ATTACK ON FLORIDA MOM SPARKS PANICKED 911 CALL: 'HER ARM IS GONE'

But with water continuing to rise, Grant called 911 to no avail, according to reports.

After Grant and her son remained stranded on the counter for hours, she decided to turn to Facebook to plead for help.

Her post caught the attention of a neighborhood mother — whose teenage sons, Lucas Marshall, 17, and Jonah Marshall, 15, set out to rescue the family using just a borrowed kayak and a paddleboard.

MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED

Jonah Marshall told ClickOrlando he didn't think twice about helping another family.

"Because they needed help, and they were in trouble and danger, so [I] just didn’t think about it and just went to help them," the teen said.

Lucas Marshall described the rescue as "nerve-wracking a little bit," but said he tried to keep Grant's son calm by striking up a conversation.

"It was good because, like, we’re physical and able to do it, so [we] might as well," he said.

"So I was just asking him, like, ‘OK, what’s your name?’" Lucas Marshall added. 

"I was like, ‘How’s school going?’ I was like, ‘This is a weird day, isn’t it?’"

The stranded mom said that she was extremely grateful for her neighbors' help.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The community came together and saved us," Grant said, according to ClickOrlando. "If it wasn’t for them, I don’t know how we would have gotten out."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Fox News Digital reached out to Grant for comment.

The flooding in Palm Bay also turned deadly Monday, when 34-year-old Joshua Bennett died after his vehicle became trapped in rising floodwaters.

His wife, Stacy Petit Bennett, told WESH 2 News he called her on FaceTime as water surrounded his vehicle.

"He called me on FaceTime, and he was just crying, like, 'I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do,'" she said.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb involved in wild catch-and-run fumble that sums up today's action
item.description: CeeDee Lamb's 10-catch, 195-yard masterclass against the Indianapolis Colts was nearly undone by a stunning fourth-quarter fumble in the red zone.
item.content:encoded:
If you have Dallas Cowboys superstar wide receiver CeeDee Lamb on your fantasy football team, congratulations (also, I hate you).

The standout pass catcher has been crushing it so far this season, sitting in the top three among all NFL wide receivers in receptions (60), yards (709), and touchdown grabs (six).

Sunday was another banner day for the five-time Pro Bowl selection, hauling in 10 catches for 195 yards and a score and proving to everyone why he is one of the best weapons in the league.

TIPS FOR YOUR FANTASY FOOTBALL DRAFT: HOW TO BUILD A WINNING TEAM WITHOUT OVERTHINKING IT

But it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows for Lamb, for as much as he helped America's Team to a victory over the Indianapolis Colts this afternoon, he had a pretty massive blunder at a critical point in the fourth quarter of the game.

Hanging onto a three-point lead and facing a third-and-12 from their own 39-yard-line, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott tossed up a prayer to his dynamic WR1 while staring down the barrel of a blitz.

Lamb plucked the ball mere inches from the ground and proceeded to stand up and run for another 25 yards.

Seems like a clutch play from a clutch player in a high leverage situation, right?

NFL STARS GO ABOVE AND BEYOND TO MAKE INCREDIBLE CATCHES DURING SUNDAY'S WEEK 5 ACTION

Watch the whole thing.

Poor CeeDee did everything right and got his team from a nearly certain punting scenario to the red zone, only to cough it all up and give the Colts a huge shot in the arm.

And for those of you wondering if Indy linebacker Austin Ajiake was the one who tripped Lamb up, thus negating the fumble by way of the ground causing it as a result of a tackle, the play was reviewed and upheld.

Colts ball, and a rare blemish on an otherwise stellar day for CeeDee.

As I mentioned, the Cowboys would end up taking the win on the road in a back-and-forth 27-23 affair, but for a moment there, it looked like CeeDee Lamb went from GOAT to sacrificial lamb in just one wacky play.

item.title: More proof that any team trading for Daniel Jones at the NFL trade deadline is chasing fool's gold
item.description: Daniel Jones threw a game-sealing interception as the Indianapolis Colts fell 27-23 to Dallas, raising major questions ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The next thing you'll hear about Daniel Jones is how the Minnesota Vikings or some other team is interested in trading for him before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday.

And the logical question a wise general manager in desperate need of a solid quarterback should be asking is: Why Daniel Jones?

Why that guy?

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

Jones plays for the Indianapolis Colts now and continues to be one of the most disappointing and under-performing reasons that team has been in garage sale mode for nearly a month, as losses increased and optimism dropped off the table.

The Colts lost again on Sunday, this time 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys, and the way this game went is a testament to why Jones is fools gold at the trade deadline.

SHANE STEICHEN SAYS DANIEL JONES WON'T BE BENCHED BUT COACH AND GENERAL MANAGER CHRIS BALLARD ARE IN TROUBLE

Jones threw an interception on the Colts' final offensive play to seal their loss.

Before that misbegotten pass, he threw an incompletion. Before that, he had an intentional grounding. And he had an incompletion before that.

The Colts had the football with 1:08 to play and needed to score a touchdown and pull out a victory. But that wasn't Dan Marino or Dan Fouts playing for the Colts.

That was Daniel Jones, who, rather than comeback wins, had mostly delivered ways to lose and disappointment during his time with the Indy and the New York Giants before that.

"Didn't finish the way we want to finish," Colts embattled head coach Shane Steichen said afterward.

Of course not, coach, your quarterback is Daniel Jones to whom you committed last season as your starter before he got hurt and crashed your season. You quarterback is Daniel Jones to whom you also committed to this year before he remained healthy and still freakin' helped crash your now 2-7 season.

Steichen will probably be fired at the end of the season for his grand commitment. And there's no telling what the next new general manager and head coach will do with Jones.

COLTS FACE QUARTERBACK UNCERTAINTY AS DANIEL JONES RECOVERS FROM ACHILLES INJURY

But that's only if Jones is still in Indy after the 4 p.m. Tuesday trade deadline.

The Minnesota Vikings reached out to the Colts in recent days about acquiring Jones.

That is significant proof that the Vikings have great confidence in their reputation for developing quarterbacks but are equally tone-deaf about their reputation for making massive mistakes in deciding what quarterbacks they want on their roster.

THE WEEK OF THE BACKUP QB IN THE NFL KICKS OFF AS SANDERS, MILTON, MINSHEW, LOCK, AND WENTZ START

The idea the Vikings or any other team might think Jones is a solution to a quarterback problem rather than a multiplication of a problem is curious. Because it forgets Jones' history of failing.

Jones threw an interception this game, and it marked the fourth consecutive game he's done that. Indeed, he's had only one game this season in which he has not thrown an interception.

And, to be fair, Jones has generally accepted responsibility for his mistakes and his role on an offense that needs to play better.

But there was a moment on Sunday when Jones seemed to blame the uncertain situation the Colts find themselves in with the deadline approaching as a reason the club's collective performance hasn't been as good as expected.

"There's been so much stuff going on and distractions and different things, and we've got to do a better job handling it as a team, collectively executing together, as a group," Jones said.

Wait.

The reason there has been so much "stuff going on" is because the club, led by Jones, has been playing poorly, which led management to begin considering the makeup of the team next year rather than the rest of this year.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

If Jones played better and the Colts won more, there wouldn't be "so much stuff going on," other than winning games.

"... We got to do a good job executing together," Jones said.

True. Jones may get a chance to do that on another team that will see him as improving their situation – kind of like the Colts did before this season began.

item.title: Iran vows ‘astonishing’ strikes and lifts missile-range limit as US targets land routes
item.description: Iran's IRGC lifted its 2,000-kilometer ballistic missile-range limit and threatened new weapons hours after U.S. Central Command launched a new task force.
item.content:encoded:
Iran lifted its self-imposed ballistic missile-range limit and threatened to unleash new, homegrown weapons that would "astonish the entire world," within hours of the U.S. military launching a new task force aimed at choking off Tehran's weapons shipments and illicit trade Nov. 7.

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi confirmed that Iran was now abandoning its previous 2,000-kilometer, or roughly 1,240-mile, ballistic missile-range restriction, according to The Associated Press.

"That restriction has been lifted for us," Mohebbi clarified in the wake of the task force announcement.

RUSSIA SECRETLY BOLSTERED IRAN'S MISSILE ARSENAL BEFORE WAR WITH US, RECORDS UNCOVER

 U.S. Central Command established "Task Force Iron Gate", an initiative targeting the movement of advanced Iranian weapons systems, dual-use materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

"Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with US Interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, said in a statement shared on X.

According to Behnam Taleblu, senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), the U.S. may now carry out "targeted strikes" against facilitators while putting "political pressure on bordering states, as well as market and sanctions pressure against institutions underwriting Iran’s illicit trade."

"It speaks volumes, of course, that this effort is being stood up within CENTCOM headquarters," Taleblu told Fox News Digital.  

Meanwhile, Iran's IRGC quickly dismissed the new initiative as "wordplay," claiming Tehran had already made preparations and coordinated with neighboring countries to withstand additional pressure, Fars News Agency reported.

Mohebbi also warned that Iran was developing new weapons capable of delivering devastating blows in another confrontation with the U.S. and Israel.

IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS

"There are surprises that will be unveiled and deployed on the battlefield if a third wave of confrontation with the enemy erupts. These surprises will astonish the entire world," Mohebbi said during a news conference in Tehran on Saturday, according to Iran's state-run Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA).

"If they once again miscalculate, or if the Zionists, in pursuit of their own interests, lead the criminal United States into another miscalculation, they should know that Iran's next blows will be even harder and will leave them crippled for years to come," he added.

Iran's previous 2,000-kilometer limit already placed the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant, most of Egypt and parts of Greece and the Balkans within range.

In March, Iran unsuccessfully attempted to strike the joint U.S.-British military base on Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, roughly 2,500 miles from the Islamic Republic.

Mohebbi also claimed Iran was preparing to unveil new underground missile facilities, as Tehran seeks to shield its weapons production from future attacks.

The installations, described by Iranian officials as "missile cities," are designed to allow the IRGC to continue manufacturing weapons during wartime, according to IRNA.

TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS

The IRGC spokesman claimed Iran's Aerospace Force continued producing missiles and drones during recent fighting, using domestic expertise without importing foreign weapons or relying on "reverse engineering of weapons captured from the enemy."

Mohebbi also described Iran's growing self-sufficiency in weapons production as a "very big achievement."

Taleblu meanwhile emphasized the significance of the Caspian Sea basin, saying the world’s largest lake has "turned into a two-way sanctions-busting hub for both Iran and Russia."

"Iranian officials always claim self-sufficiency in their military industries," he said.

"But with domestic missile production significantly constrained due to the 40-Day War, the regime will be reliant on imports to build back, and especially at scale and at a faster rate.

"This is why efforts to constrain both land and sea trade in and out of Iran are a one-two punch for the regime."

The warnings come as Washington intensified pressure on Iran's regional trade routes, including its land crossings with Iraq, where Baghdad has reportedly resisted U.S. demands for full and broader border restrictions.

According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Iraq has closed only one border crossing with Iran so far, despite reported American pressure to shut down most crossings between the two countries.

FRESH ACTIVITY EMERGES AT IRAN’S DEEPLY BURIED NUCLEAR SITE AS TRUMP WARNS IRAN NOT TO ‘GET CUTE’

On Sunday, the U.S. Treasury pressed Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except for two as part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said, according to Reuters.

The Iraqi government had closed the al-Shayeb crossing in southeastern Iraq on Oct. 21, to review security and install equipment to prevent smuggling of prohibited materials.

Iraqi political sources told Agence France-Presse that Washington had pressured Baghdad to close most Iran-Iraq border crossings to restrict trade and financial exchanges that could help Tehran withstand U.S. sanctions, ISW reported.

ISW also said that Iranian Ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh was pressuring tribal leaders in Iraq's Maysan province to push Iraqi officials and leaders of the Shiite Coordination Framework to reopen al-Shayeb.

Al-Sadegh is reportedly a member of the IRGC's Quds Force, which oversees the organization's foreign operations.

The institute assessed that Baghdad's limited response likely reflects efforts to balance its relationship with Washington against the influence of Iranian-backed political factions.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders makes case to replace Deshaun Watson despite Browns' overtime loss to Saints
item.description: Shedeur Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints, but his receivers did much of the heavy lifting in Cleveland's OT loss.
item.content:encoded:
For most of Sunday's game, Shedeur Sanders looked a lot like Deshaun Watson (with regard to his play, not the ... other stuff).

But a few key plays, including one of the best throws of Sanders' young career to help set up a game-tying field goal, are likely to have Browns fans demanding that the team turn the keys over to the 24-year-old son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Sanders finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints. Those numbers look pretty good, but they also make his afternoon look quite a bit better than it actually was.

Which, again, sounds a lot like Watson's season.

Sanders got his first start of the year after Watson entered the concussion protocol during the week. Watson cleared the protocol Saturday, but the Browns still made him inactive Sunday. Head coach Todd Monken had already named Sanders the starter Friday after Watson was unable to participate in team reps during the week.

That gave Sanders, who started seven games as a rookie last season, another chance to prove he deserves to be the team's starter moving forward. For much of the afternoon, he didn't do a whole lot with it.

Sanders threw for just 38 yards in the first half and was sacked five times for a loss of 37 yards on the day. He didn't look entirely comfortable, and some of those sacks were particularly costly. Cleveland's first two goal-to-go possessions produced three points, with Sanders taking a sack on each.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The second of those opportunities came courtesy of a tremendous effort by Browns receiver Denzel Boston. Sanders underthrew a wide-open Boston down the sideline, but Boston adjusted to the throw, snatched it over the defender and then took it inside the Saints' 5-yard line for a 60-yard completion.

After a run went backward, Sanders took a seven-yard sack that pushed Cleveland back to the 12. The Browns settled for a field goal.

With Cleveland trailing 9-6 in the fourth quarter, Sanders found KC Concepcion for a 64-yard score. It was a huge play that gave the Browns the lead with 5:21 remaining, but Concepcion was wide open on what appeared to be a blown coverage by New Orleans. Concepcion caught the pass at the Saints' 28-yard line, then made a nice move to cut back across the field to outrun two Saints defenders into the end zone.

Sanders deserves credit for finding the wide-open Concepcion and delivering a catchable ball that gave him room to work. But it was a throw that every NFL quarterback should be able to make.

Cleveland then had a chance to run out the clock and win in regulation after its defense forced a punt. Sanders picked up a first down with his legs, but a holding penalty and another sack helped derail the possession. New Orleans got the ball back and scored a touchdown to take a 16-13 lead with 58 seconds left.

Facing third-and-6 from his own 30 on the ensuing drive, Sanders moved outside the pocket and fired a 30-yard strike to Jerry Jeudy while taking a massive hit from Chase Young. It was easily his best throw of the afternoon and one of the best of his young NFL career. It was probably the best throw by a Browns quarterback this season, too.

Sanders eventually led the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's 51-yard field goal, which tied the game with eight seconds remaining and forced the game to overtime.

The Browns won the toss and elected to kick, something I've repeatedly said is the wrong decision for NFL teams. Cleveland ignored my advice, and New Orleans promptly marched 74 yards in 11 plays for a touchdown.

Sanders answered by completing six of eight passes on a 67-yard touchdown drive. Harold Fannin Jr., though, deserves most of the credit for the play that brought Cleveland within a point.

Fannin caught a short pass just beyond the line of scrimmage, broke multiple tackles and turned it into a 39-yard touchdown.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Cleveland went for a two-point conversion and the win, but the New Orleans pass rush immediately pressured Sanders. He scrambled to his right before throwing an incomplete pass intended for Boston, ending the game.

Boston's catch, Concepcion's touchdown and Fannin's catch-and-run accounted for 163 of Sanders' 297 passing yards. His receivers did a lot of work to make that final line look as good as it did.

Before Sunday's game, Monken said he assumed Watson would remain the starter when healthy. But Watson hasn't exactly done enough to cement his status as the Browns' starting quarterback.

Cleveland entered Sunday at 5-3, with all five victories coming by four points or fewer. Their record has made Watson's season look better than his actual play.

Sanders showed plenty of the same problems Sunday. He also delivered a terrific throw when the Browns desperately needed one and helped put them in position to win in overtime.

If the Browns are going to get uneven quarterback play no matter who starts, it's fair to ask why the 24-year-old shouldn't be the one getting the opportunity to develop through it.

item.title: You better not dare be smoking in Broncos head coach Sean Payton's postgame news conference
item.description: Sean Payton mistook a reporter's pencil for a cigarette during his postgame presser after the Denver Broncos' Mile High City win over the Panthers.
item.content:encoded:
Things are going pretty well for the folks in the Mile High City when it comes to their football team.

The Denver Broncos are fresh off a trip to the AFC Championship game less than a year ago, and this year's team is off to a 7-2 start as they lead the pack in a competitive AFC West division.

A lot of that is due to the wizardry of head coach Sean Payton, who came onto the scene in Denver in 2023 and turned a franchise that had not been to the playoffs since winning Super Bowl 50 nearly a decade ago into a legitimate contender.

Payton's no nonsense approach to coaching coupled with his offensive acumen seems to have been the panacea for a Broncos team in limbo for much of the late 2010s and early 2020s.

That no nonsense approach apparently extends to the beat reporters in Denver, too.

BRONCOS COACH SEAN PAYTON BURIES GEOFF SCHWARTZ AFTER ANALYST BUTCHERS BO NIX'S DOWNFIELD GAME

After the Broncos' 26-21 win over the then-AFC South-leading Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon, Payton took the podium to discuss the victory before taking exception to a reporter apparently daring to have a smoke right in the middle of his postgame press conference.

There's just one problem: the reporter in question wasn't taking a drag off a Marlboro Red but was just chomping on a good old Dixon Ticonderoga No. 2 pencil.

As a man who lost his father-in-law to lung cancer a few years back, I have to commend Coach Payton's stance on smoking, but this was an absolutely wild interaction.

You can tell Payton was pretty embarrassed about the whole thing too, but fortunately both he and the reporter took the exchange in stride.

MIKE MACDONALD APOLOGIZES TO SEAN PAYTON FOR REVEALING SPYGATE-TYPE ACCUSATIONS BETWEEN BRONCOS AND SEAHAWKS

The Super Bowl-winning head coach could barely make it through his answer without busting out in laughter.

The good news here is that when Payton decides it's time to hang up the visor and whistle, he has a career as a D.A.R.E. officer at any school district in either the Denver or New Orleans areas.

"Hey kids, I'm officer Sean, and I don't care if you're a Super Bowl champion or a Broncos beat writer, I better not EVER catch you smoking or doing drugs! That's not what winners do."

Let this be a lesson to anyone trying to sneak an E-Cig into a postgame presser moving forward: just say "NO."

item.title: Elon Musk’s Austin home targeted by well-funded leftist groups aboard party buses
item.description: Three far-left nonprofits with $56.1 million in combined revenue organized a theatrical protest outside Elon Musk's Austin-area home
item.content:encoded:
Three far-left nonprofits with combined annual revenues of $56.1 million escalated their protests against SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk this week by targeting his Austin-area home with a seemingly innocuous post-election "party" featuring two chartered buses, music, speeches, theatrical Cybertruck piñatas and dancing to Queen’s "We Will Rock You."

The event’s organizers – VOCAL-TX, the fiscally-sponsored project of a New York 501(c)(3) nonprofit; the Center for Popular Democracy Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Brooklyn; and People’s Action, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit based in Chicago – framed the Saturday event as a tame "People Over Billionaires Election After Party."

The demonstration reflected growing coordination among leftist networks worldwide, from Paris to Portland, Ore., supplying organizers, transportation, coalition partners, event platforms, messaging and other logistical support for actions presented as "grassroots." As Democratic politicians threaten investigations into Trump’s corporate backers, including Musk, the street protests help create the appearance of bottom-up support.

The leaders of the organizations behind the "After Party," held in West Lake Hills, Tex., where Musk owns a sprawling home, didn’t provide comment in response to queries from Fox News Digital, but they have insisted in the past that their local protests are the result of "organic" organizing in communities.

A now-ubiquitous, mass-produced anti-Musk "I AM STEALING FROM YOU" poster, featuring the tech billionaire with creepy eyes, has appeared at demonstrations nationwide and was also on display at the Austin protest outside his home.

WHO’S FUNDING AMERICA’S PROTEST UNREST? FOX NATION'S NEW 'RIOT INC.' FOLLOWS THE MONEY TO FIND OUT

This weekend’s organizers helped lead the "Tesla Takedown" protests that sometimes turned ugly last year. According to a Fox News Digital investigation, 258 organizations with combined annual revenues of an estimated $2.6 billion were behind those protests.

At Saturday’s event, participants arrived at the property in two blue Fly-Rides party buses and additional vehicles. Organizers blasted music including Queen’s "We Will Rock You," over loudspeakers.

"We'll bring the music, you bring the dance moves! This is family friendly, peaceful and FUN event!" the organizers wrote, promoting the event.

The Austin American-Statesman covered the event and cast it playfully, with the headline "Dozens party outside Elon Musk's West Lake Hills home after campaign donations fell flat." It wrote about how organizers led a "Love Train" conga line and distributed party hats and refreshments, including cider.

The organizations behind the campaign are veterans of the professional protest industry. While this event was peaceful, the rhetoric of demonization and polarization at protests causes researchers at organizations like the Network Contagion Research Institute to conclude that that they can create a "permission structure" for political violence.

‘ASTROTURF’: CRITICS SPECULATE TESLA PROTESTS ARE NOT A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT, BUT A CAREFULLY ORGANIZED CAMPAIGN

The three nonprofits behind this weekend’s protests are part of a powerful national tax-exempt nonprofit industry that has increasingly taken to the streets over the past decade in coordinated, orchestrated campaigns in local communities, creating the image of homegrown organic demonstrations.

The three groups reported $56.1 million in combined 2024 revenue, according to their most recent tax filings.

Organizers promoted the event as a peaceful celebration of voters rejecting the influence of wealthy donors. About 60 people attended, according to estimates.

The demonstration followed in the spirit of the very coordinated "Tesla Takedown" protests launched at Texas dealerships in early 2025, when activists organized demonstrations against Tesla and Musk over his political activities and role in the new Trump administration and the Department of Government Efficiency, called DOGE. Those protests led to vandalism against Tesla vehicles and dealerships. A wider network of openly pro-communist groups, including Freedom Road Socialist Organization, carried posters with messages like "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES. WE NEED SOCIALISM."

Congressional lawmakers and Justice Department prosecutors are investigating an American-born, Shanghai-based tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, for funding and backing pro-communist groups. Some of those groups, including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, ANSWER Coalition, CodePink and People's Forum, have supported the regular protests that have hit America's streets, including the anti-Musk demonstrations.

.

DEMOCRATS SET SIGHTS ON ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER MIDTERM WINS, BUT PRITZKER DRAWS A SURPRISING LINE

Much like the networks behind "No Kings," "Hands Off," "ICE Out" and other protests over the past year, the financial filings of the organizations behind this weekend’s demonstration show the scale of the infrastructure behind these groups.

The Center for Popular Democracy reported $40.9 million in 2024 revenue. People’s Action Institute reported $2.1 million, and Voices of Community Activists and Leaders Inc., or VOCAL-NY, which fiscally sponsors VOCAL-TX, reported $13.1 million. The organizations are separate entities, and the figures don’t represent a shared operating budget.

VOCAL-TX’s donation page identifies VOCAL-NY as its 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor and sister organization. VOCAL-NY describes the organization as a statewide grassroots membership group focused on "building the power of low-income people" impacted by "HIV/AIDS, drug policy, mass incarceration, the war on drugs and homelessness." It says its work is "accomplished through community organizing, campaigns & harm reduction services."

The Center for Popular Democracy Inc. lists VOCAL-TX among its affiliates and describes itself as a network of "grassroots" organizations operating across dozens of states, building a "representative, multiracial society and government where all thrive, no exceptions," according to its nonprofit mission statement.

SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

The Center for Popular Democracy reported $38.2 million in contributions and $14.6 million in other salaries and compensation in 2024. Its two co-executive directors received an average total compensation of $234,026, including bonuses in 2024, according to their latest tax filings, about four times more than the $63,360 median annual earnings of full-time, year-round U.S. workers that year.

VOCAL-NY reported nearly $3.5 million in other salaries and wages and listed its Texas co-director among its highest-paid employees, earning $113,842 in salary and $21,854 in bonuses in 2024.

People’s Action describes itself as a national network of grassroots groups "organized to promote economic, racial and social equity through national, regional and local advocacy campaigns."

Saturday’s gathering transformed a political victory "party" into a theatrical public spectacle, using buses, coordinated messaging, music and symbolic props to deliver a broader message: that billionaire wealth shouldn’t determine the direction of American politics. Protesters didn't specifically address the millionaires and billionaires that funnel money to Democratic politicians such as George Soros, Reid Hoffman and Pierre Omidyar, to name just a few.

Participants carried signs reading "Texas is not for sale" and "Alright Texas! Now let’s tax Musk." Attendees also smashed star-shaped and piñatas shaped like a Tesla Cybertruck.

CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

Eli Cortez, a VOCAL-TX bus captain, told attendees that the event was intended to celebrate voters rejecting the political influence of billionaires, according to coverage by the Austin American-Statesman. Cortez didn’t respond to a request for comment.

The demonstration focused on Musk’s spending during the 2026 election cycle. A New York Times analysis placed Musk’s total disclosed political spending at approximately $474 million, while other analyses based more narrowly on Federal Election Commission filings put the figure at roughly $445 million. About $212 million supported Texas Republican Ken Paxton’s unsuccessful Senate campaign through allied political committees.

May Day Strong, another far-left coalition tagged in the social media promotion of the event, describes itself as a "constellation" of more than 600 labor and community organizations, many of them socialist and communist. Its stated demands include taxing the rich, opposing ICE, expanding "democracy" and organizing workers to "protest, refuse to comply, and take the economic actions" needed to oppose the Trump administration.

Austin protesters carried a trademark poster with a creepy image of Musk and the message, "I Am Stealing From You," now a mainstay at protests, not as a spontaneous grassroots creation but a strategic asset. The Progressive Change Institute, the 501(c)(3) sister organization of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, has taken credit for commissioning the art early last year by Washington, D.C., political street artist Absurdly Well.

The graphic became part of the propaganda of the broader "Hands Off" protest network, which distributed thousands of copies of the poster. CNN, the Associated Press, the New York Times, Axios, TIME, Reuters, The Hill and MSNBC host Rachel Maddow have splashed photos of the poster in its coverage Progressive Change Campaign Committee's online member engagement director has said the merchandise was intended to serve an organizing purpose beyond fundraising, with the goal of making Elon Musk "a real liability for the administration."

The group now gives donors "5- or 10-pack of anti-Elon Musk rally posters" in exchange for donations: $135 for a five-pack, $250 for a $10-pack and $30 for a single poster.

At least two of the iconic posters landed in the "party" protest outside Musk's home, held overhead by demonstrators.

Burrow threw three touchdown passes and ran for another touchdown in a convincing 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons.

Because Burrow is on fire.

He has accounted for 18 touchdowns in his last four games.

He's thrown for 1,215 yards in those four games.

ZAC TAYLOR FACES MAKE-OR-BREAK SEASON AS BENGALS REBUILD DEFENSE AROUND JOE BURROW'S SUPER BOWL WINDOW

His passer rating is 132.0 in those four combined games.

"I loved putting on a show for the people of Spain and was happy to be here," Burrow said afterward in English.

"We've just played together for so long now," Burrow said. "We're coming up on 10 years playing together. So, you know, when you do that, you develop that connection mentally that nothing needs to be said."

WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG

Their marriage has made headlines in recent years as the couple has spoken publicly about their decision to live separately at different points in their relationship.

"Literally our marriage was going down like the Titanic, and Billy moved 50 yards away from me in the guest house and so far, so good," Phillips said in an Instagram video.

"It's kind of working. I'm not really sure what's going to come of it but hey, I'm not fighting it."

"Bijou and Mackenzie spent a lot more time together than I did with them. I was basically raised as an only child, but as I matured and grew older, I reached out more to them, and we all started spending more time together and now we're inseparable."

item.title: Video shows small plane clip pickup truck during emergency landing on busy Florida road
item.description: Video captures a small plane making an emergency landing on a North Fort Myers road, clipping a pickup truck as it touches down on the asphalt.
item.content:encoded:
A small plane turned a Florida road into an emergency runway Saturday, crashing into the back of a moving pickup truck in a dramatic close call captured on video.

Two pilots were aboard the aircraft when a mechanical issue forced them to attempt an emergency landing near Bayshore Road and Interstate 75 in North Fort Myers around noon, according to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office.

The plane departed Sebring, Florida, around 11 a.m. Saturday and made the emergency landing about 50 minutes later, at 11:50 a.m., according to FlightAware tracking data.

DASHCAM VIDEO CAPTURES SMALL PLANE CRASHING ON SAN JOSE HIGHWAY, INJURING THREE ON BOARD, INCLUDING CHILD

Video captured from the road shows the plane’s wheels touch down on the asphalt as it speeds along Bayshore Road, its wing clipping the rear of a pickup traveling in the same direction.

The truck was heading eastbound when the aircraft struck it, according to the sheriff’s office. No injuries were reported.

Images shared by the sheriff’s office show the aftermath, with the small aircraft sitting on the roadway.

"Thankfully, this incident had a positive outcome, and no one was injured," Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said in a statement.

NTSB FINDS 'NO EVIDENCE' OF MAR-A-LAGO CONNECTION AFTER FLORIDA JET CRASH KILLS NINE PEOPLE

"Given the recent tragic news involving aviation accidents, we are especially grateful that everyone is safe."

Marceno credited patrol deputies, FDOT Southwest Florida and Bayshore Fire Rescue for their quick response.

PILOTS' PUSH TO LEVEL JET MAY HAVE TORN OFF KEY PIECE FOUND MILES FROM FLORIDA CRASH, FORMER NTSB EXPERT SAYS

"We will continue working closely with our partners at the FAA as they review the circumstances surrounding this incident," he said.

The Federal Aviation Administration is leading the investigation, according to the sheriff’s office.

PRIVATE JET WITH 9 PEOPLE ON BOARD CRASHES JUST MILES FROM MAR-A-LAGO

The close call came less than a week after a Learjet crashed Sunday, Nov. 1, in Greenacres in Palm Beach County, killing all nine people aboard.

Federal investigators are working to determine what caused that crash.

item.title: Week 10 AP Poll sees Georgia rightfully take over top spot while voters continue to award USC for no reason
item.description: Georgia jumped to No. 1 after dismantling Ole Miss 42-7, while the Alabama-Tennessee ranking debate and USC's puzzling rise stir controversy.
item.content:encoded:
Week 10 had the potential to be one of the more chaotic and disruptive weekends of the college football season, with seven ranked-on-ranked matchups. Naturally, five of those seven matchups were won by the favorite, and instead of a weekend resulting in chaos, it was a weekend of teams making statements.

It's always the loaded slates that hardly ever meet expectations, and the weekends you least expect that deliver the goods.

No team sent a stronger statement on Saturday than the Georgia Bulldogs with their 42-7 dismantling of Ole Miss on the road, and they were rewarded with the No. 1 being added next to their name. The Dawgs and Rebels each threw for 186 yards in the game, but all was not equal on the ground, as Georgia dominated both lines of scrimmage and picked up 295 rushing yards compared to Ole Miss' 66 yards on the ground.

Perhaps the biggest stunner from Week 10 is that AP voters finally got things right, at least for the most part.

Yes, they caught a break with the mostly chalk results and a lack of difficult decisions to make, but for as much as we love to pile it on when the poll is a disaster, we have to tip our cap on the rare occasion that the poll makes a lot of sense.

Georgia may have a loss, unlike the two unbeatens of Utah and UCLA, but there is no reality where someone could watch what the Bulldogs did to Ole Miss on Saturday night and not tab them as the No. 1 team in the country.

If anyone wants to waste energy arguing about how UCLA and Utah should both be ranked ahead of one-loss Notre Dame, they can have at it.

Just like there isn't a world where Georgia shouldn't be ranked No. 1, there also isn't a world where voters were going to put both Utah and UCLA ahead of the Fighting Irish after they knocked off Miami.

Notre Dame couldn't stay put at No. 4 after beating the team that the same voters had ranked No. 1 in the country one week ago. And no, it does not matter that Miami's best player, Malachi Toney, did not play.

ALABAMA FINALLY PUTS IT ALL TOGETHER, DOMINATES LSU AND LEAVES LANE KIFFIN STARING AT $40 MILLION CFP DISASTER

Is Alabama being ranked No. 7 and Tennessee being ranked No. 9 that big of a deal? No, none of this is with the College Football Playoff Rankings taking all precedence, but Vols fans have every right to be frustrated with the Tide being ranked ahead of them.

Alabama and Tennessee are both 7-2 on the season, and with the Volunteers beating the Crimson Tide by 16 points earlier this season, the 'tiebreaker' should go Tennessee's way. On top of that, Tennessee dominated then No. 8 Kentucky 34-6 in Week 10.

NO 3 UTAH REMAINS UNDEFEATED WITH THRILLING WIN OVER NO 9 BYU BEHIND HEISMAN FINALIST DEVON DAMPIER'S EPIC DAY

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Alabama going to Baton Rouge and beating up on then No. 15 LSU on Saturday can't and shouldn't be ignored, but with Tennessee winning the head-to-head and having the more impressive win on paper, it doesn't make much sense to have the Vols ranked behind the Tide this week.

Tennessee fans can also point a (small) finger at Texas in this situation as well. The Longhorns beat Tennessee in Knoxville, hence their ranking ahead of the Vols, and with voters having to rank these teams somewhere, Texas really not being able to fall anywhere other than No. 8 adds another wrinkle to the mess.

If we got into all the resumes, hypotheticals, and head-to-head matchups, we'd be here all day.

We pointed out last week that the Trojans were getting way too much love from the voters, moving up to the No. 18 spot after knocking off what we now know is a very mediocre Ohio State team.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

This week, USC was on a bye, and its signature win against the Buckeyes looks even worse with Ohio State losing to Oregon, yet the Trojans moved up three spots to No. 15 by simply not playing.

I'd say make it make sense, but it doesn't. USC has one notable win against a now three-loss Buckeyes team and losses to Oregon and Wisconsin. That is not the resume of a Top 15 team in the country.

Actual reality will fall into place in Week 11 when the Trojans travel to Bloomington to take on No. 6 Indiana in a monster matchup.

Sydney Thomas mocked LSU head coach Lane Kiffin before Halloween with a joke about dressing up as him losing to Ole Miss. The costume idea, for whatever reason, ended up not making the cut this year.

item.title: Independent wrestling's heart still beating even as social media begins to write its obituary
item.description: Ben Bishop and Killer Kross dismiss claims that independent wrestling is dead after Fight Factory's No Thanks Given drew hundreds in New Jersey.
item.content:encoded:
The pro wrestling conversation on social media usually ranges from hotly contested debates between which company is better, WWE or AEW, fans complaining about the way their favorite wrestler is booked or there being too many commercials on TV. OK, maybe the last one is just me tweeting into the void.

Regardless, there was a lot of chatter online about independent wrestling being "dead." The noise around the notion appeared to spark when Produce Wrestling and Absolute Intense Wrestling (AIW) announced hiatuses for different reasons for the end of the year. For what it’s worth, Produce already has a show booked for Feb. 25.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

OutKick Dropkick has put the spotlight on several independent shows this year with a few different promotions, including Pandemonium Pro Wrestling, Awesome Championship Wrestling, Produce Wrestling, Gamechanger Wrestling, Fight Factory Wrestling and others. So, as social media wrote an obituary for the indies, OutKick Dropkick made its way to Middletown, New Jersey, on Friday night to take in Fight Factory’s No Thanks Given and to see whether the vibes would be more of a concert or a wake. It didn’t disappoint.

Ben Bishop, who made a surprise appearance at Total Nonstop Action Wrestling’s (TNA) Bound for Glory pay-per-view assembled a team for an elimination eight-person tag team match against MADE. Richard Holliday, Jack Vaughn and Madisyn Maxwell went up against Made. Kristin Blaze then defeated Rachel Ley in a preview of what women’s wrestling may look like in the future. Even WWE Hall of Famer Arn Anderson showed up to support his sons as they took on Sent 2 Salute.

The main event featured a no holds barred match between TNA star KC Navarro and Steve Gibki for the latter’s openweight championship. The match ended with Gibki spearing Navarro through a table and putting his opponent in the Hell Hammer for the win.

The show was held at the Middletown Sports Complex, which is not a large venue by any means. But pro wrestling fans still showed up to fill the available seats. Most lasted through the chilly conditions since the event took place on a literal ice rink, which is also the home of the North American Hockey League’s New Jersey Titans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

There certainly was no funeral for independent wrestling. In fact, attendees were actively engaged in the sport that was happening in and outside of the ring.

OutKick Dropkick asked Bishop whether he believed the indies were dead.

"I mean, look at it, look at it here. In Middletown, New Jersey, on a Friday night, you could be doing anything," Bishop said. "We're close to (New York City). There's a ton of things you can do. We got about 300, almost 400-plus here in Middletown, New Jersey, here at Fight Factory. You can thank me for the house. So yeah, this whole notion, indies are dead, all that stuff, it's just words, it's just noise. It comes up every few months. Everyone wants to pretend that they think that when they were wrestling on the indies, it was so much better. It is what it is. Things evolve, things change. I believe that indie wrestling is alive and well."

Bishop is right.

Anyone who was in the facility on Friday night could have been doing anything else. WWE’s "Friday Night SmackDown" was on TV, "World of Warcraft’s" new game just dropped, there was basketball and hockey going on at the same time.

And maybe you don’t know who Ben Bishop is. Maybe you didn’t see his "curtain call" with Holliday, Vaughn and Tommy Invincible at War on the Shore 3 that had social media talking over the summer. And all of that is OK.

OutKick Dropkick asked Killer Kross his thoughts about the same notion. Kross works for a big-time company in Major League Wrestling, which has multiple media rights deals and partnerships with CMLL and New Japan Pro-Wrestling. However, he’s gone on his own tours in the U.S. and abroad for promotions big and small.

Kross said he wasn’t necessarily plugged into the conversation but suggested that the attendance at independent events undercut the notion that independent wrestling is dying.

"No, that's hilarious to me," he said. "These are people who don't attend indies that are saying that, and I don't even think they're saying it to be malicious. I think they're just innocently saying it because You know, when, when you're a young adult and you have a very busy life, if you're not paying attention to something, or like you're not paying attention to the big main thing that everybody's paying attention to, then you innocently will think that it's not important cause it doesn't have your attention.

Pro wrestlers who aren’t exclusively signed to the major corporate companies are working their tails off to make a living in their sport and to put on a good show for those who do come out and see them.

Not every venue is going to be Allegiant Stadium or Wembley Stadium. The pro wrestlers who work these shows know that and work together to put on the best matches they can to keep the fans coming back for more.

Is independent wrestling dying? No chance.

item.title: Alanis Morissette identifies as pansexual, months after reflecting on Sarah Jessica Parker 'SATC' kiss
item.description: Alanis Morissette revealed she is pansexual on the "Handsome" podcast, joking she likes to "confuse people on the way out" with such revelations.
item.content:encoded:
Alanis Morissette’s recent decision to publicly identify as pansexual has cast her famous same-sex kiss with Sarah Jessica Parker on "Sex and the City" in a new light.

The singer, 52, opened up about her sexuality during an appearance on the "Handsome" podcast after previously discussing the memorable 2000 scene on Alex Cooper’s "Call Her Daddy" podcast in September.

Morissette appeared on "Sex and the City" in the season 3 episode "Boy, Girl, Boy, Girl…" as Dawn, a woman who kisses Parker’s character, Carrie Bradshaw, during a game of spin the bottle.

ALANIS MORISSETTE SAYS WEBSITES WERE BUILT TO PLOT HER MURDER AFTER 'JAGGED LITTLE PILL' SUCCESS

During her September appearance on "Call Her Daddy," Morissette revealed that she helped pitch the storyline to the show’s producers.

"I reached out to them and I said, ‘Might it be a nice time for Carrie to experience a lesbian moment?’" Morissette said. "And they said, ‘Why, yes. We were thinking the same thing.’"

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I think we literally had the same idea at the same time," she added. "That happens."

Morissette also reflected on the kiss itself, describing the moment with Parker as "easy" and "buoyant."

"I do recall kissing her," she said. "It was very pleasant."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Morissette’s comments resurfaced after she publicly identified as pansexual during Tuesday’s episode of the "Handsome" podcast, co-hosted by Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster and Mae Martin.

The conversation turned to the singer’s rocky dating history with men.

"I’m sorry for the men that hurt you, but I’m not sorry for the songs that came from it," Feimster told Morissette before asking, "Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?"

"I’m pansexual, so, yeah," Morissette replied.

"Wait, you’re not really pansexual, are you?" Notaro asked.

"I am," Morissette confirmed.

"You’re supposed to come into the ‘Handsome’ podcast leading with, ‘I’m pansexual,’" Notaro said.

"You know, I like to leave it for the epilogue," Morissette responded. "I like to confuse people on the way out."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Morissette previously spoke about sexuality during a 2008 interview with The Advocate.

"I think it’s a beautiful rite of passage for everyone to play with their sexuality at some point, so I did exactly that," she said. "And it was great!"

"I’ve felt love from the gay community since I was really young because all my friends were gay," Morissette added. "There’s a passion, a presence, and a curiosity with a lot of gay people that I meet, and that aliveness is such a special quality to me."

item.title: Steve Sarkisian has already started his campaign for Texas Longhorns with ridiculous 'big game' comments
item.description: Steve Sarkisian claimed nobody believed Texas would win at Missouri, pushing an underdog narrative despite the Longhorns' 34-20 road victory.
item.content:encoded:
When SEC programs hire head coaches, a key part of their interview process must be testing their ability to do marketing and promotion.

Few, if any, coaches excel at marketing, like LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin, who has worked tirelessly to convince the broader college football public that losing games should not be punished because of SEC stadiums. Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea campaigned in 2025 by telling fans, voters and media that SEC teams should be given preferential treatment over all other conferences if they have the same records.

Then there's Steve Sarkisian.

SUDDENLY, STEVE SARKISIAN IS SINGING A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT TUNE ABOUT PLAYING OHIO STATE

The Texas Longhorns head coach said in 2025 that excluding his 9-3 team from the College Football Playoff would be a "disservice to the sport." A disservice! College football would forever be lesser if a 9-3 Texas team was not included, despite several awful performances against a bad Florida team, a bad Mississippi State team, a bad Kentucky team, and getting blown out by Georgia.

Sark complained about the result of the 2025 matchup between the Longhorns and Ohio State Buckeyes hurt his team's resume, saying that even in a 14-7 loss, Texas shouldn't be punished for scheduling a tough opponent. There's some truth to that, sure, but after their miraculous comeback in this year's game, he had a totally different perspective.

"We could be like other teams and play Jones Junior High and win 66-0," he said to reporters after beating OSU. "I don’t know what that does for us. Tonight we found out that we can (win big games)."

When they lose, the result shouldn't matter. When they win, it's a huge boost to their resume compared to teams that played lesser opponents. Shocking.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL FANS AND MEDIA RIP SEC REFS OVER CONTROVERSIAL FORWARD FUMBLE CALL IN TEXAS-MISSOURI GAME

Well, Sark is back, and this time, the marketing effort is to convince those watching that the Longhorns are actually humble little "nobody believes in us" underdogs. Against Missouri.

"I'm really proud of our football team overall because our guys, they're not naive to noise. As much as I would love to say, tune it all out — and we try our best to do that — I could hear the talk getting on the plane yesterday. I could hear the talk when we got here," he said after their 34-20 win. "Nobody believed we'd win the game. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we'd be pushed around."

He continued, saying that the "DNA" of Texas is "toughness," which showed through against the Tigers.

"The DNA of this organization is mental and physical toughness, and I think that poured out of our pores today in this ball game today, and so I'm very proud of them for that. I'm very proud of the way they hung together, the way they responded to adversity," Sarkisian said.

And finally, claimed that the win showed they're "big game hunters."

"We are big game hunters, and we showed up again today," he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Sure! It was a good win for Texas, on the road against a solid, top-25 level opponent. They did face some "adversity," mainly falling behind after a shaky first quarter, then fighting their way back. But acting as though Texas, literally Texas, with arguably the most expensive roster in the sport, or at worst, top 2-3, is a "nobody believed in us" team is ridiculous. Beyond ridiculous.

Texas also had some help, well, a lot of help from the officials. A number of questionable calls went against the Tigers, including what appeared to be a completed pass on a big third down deep in Texas territory, and what seemed like a clear incomplete pass from Arch Manning on 3rd-and-10 being ruled a fumble that gave the Longhorns a 12-yard gain and a first down. Sure enough, that drive resulted in a touchdown and what wound up being 21 unanswered points.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

That's not to say officiating was the reason Texas won, but it sure didn't hurt. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz implied as much after the game, when asked about the number of calls that went against his team.

"If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that. I'm not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team," he said, according to On3.

Even the announcing team, including Jesse Palmer, were flabbergasted at the officiating.

"If you're a Missouri fan, if you're Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today," he said.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Again, this isn't to say Texas didn't deserve to win, they outplayed Missouri on the field and were the better team. It's the attitude that Sarkisian brings, that they were just humble underdogs clinging to a win against the big, bad Missouri Tigers that's the marketing campaign.

By acting as though every win his team gets is a monumental achievement, it builds the case that should Texas trip up against, say, a struggling LSU or on the road against a bad Texas A&M team, they can't be punished for it. It's marketing. It's classic SEC. And it's ridiculous.

item.title: JJ McCarthy left Giants game with hip injury, putting Jameis Winston in the lineup but that isn't whole story
item.description: J.J. McCarthy left the Giants-Eagles game with a hip injury after a hit from Zack Baun, forcing New York to turn the offense back to Jameis Winston.
item.content:encoded:
J.J. McCarthy had two basic issues during his time with the Minnesota Vikings: Ability. And durability.

Since his trade to the New York Giants, McCarthy has shown no ability problems because he beat out Jameis Winston as the team's starter and even provided something of a spark in helping New York beat the Houston Texans in overtime.

So no ability issue.

But Sunday presented a durability issue.

McCarthy left the game against the Philadelphia Eagles with what the team is saying is a hip injury.

PATRICK MAHOMES SUFFERS APPARENT ELBOW INJURY ON THROWING ARM BUT RETURNS TO FACE THE NEW YORK JETS

So, back to Jameis Winston for the Giants.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Winston entered the game on the Giants’ first possession of the third quarter after McCarthy took a shot from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. McCarthy gingerly got himself to the New York sideline and took a knee.

McCarthy tried to throw a warmup pass after collecting himself and could be seen writhing in pain during the follow-through.

OutKick and FOX News Digital medical expert said the tape of the play suggests an oblique muscle injury. The Giants say McCarthy is questionable to return. .

McCarthy completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards before he departed. He was sacked five times in the first half.

He returned to the sideline and was seen encouraging his teammates as if he intended to return to the game. 

Despite what appeared to be too much pain to function, McCarthy returned to the game in the fourth quarter. It is possible he agreed to take a shot to deaden the pain and return.

item.title: Deputy White House Chief of Staff Richard Walters exits job ahead of Stephen Miller takeover
item.description: Stephen Miller praised Richard Walters as an “invaluable member" who will continue helping the administration from outside the White House.
item.content:encoded:
White House Deputy Chief of Staff Richard Walters, a longtime ally of outgoing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, is leaving the Trump administration following President Donald Trump's decision to replace Wiles with Stephen Miller.

Miller confirmed Walters' departure in a statement to Fox News, describing him as an "invaluable member" of the White House who will continue to assist the administration from the outside.

"Richard has been an invaluable member of the White House and has helped deliver some of the Administration’s biggest victories. While he will be leaving us, Richard will continue to help from the outside as we continue to work with all of our strength to deliver for President Trump and his courageous fight to Save America," Miller said.

The move ends Walters' months-long tenure in the role, which he was appointed to in May 2026, according to LegiStorm. Walters previously served as executive director of the inaugural committee for Trump and Vice President JD Vance, according to Georgetown University, where he was a fellow at the Institute of Politics and Public Service.

TRUMP NAMES STEPHEN MILLER NEW WHITE HOUSE CHIEF OF STAFF, REPLACING SUSIE WILES

The departure marks the first major staff turnover as Miller prepares to install his own leadership team when he takes over Monday. The move is part of a broader effort by Trump to overhaul his administration following the midterm elections, in which Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate.

Miller's wife, Katie, on Sunday also announced that she would stop recording new episodes of her show, The Katie Miller Podcast, where she interviews political figures, athletes and other public personalities.

She said the decision was based on what was best for her children and family as her husband's new role brings a shift in priorities.

HEGSETH'S FUTURE DRAWS OMINOUS PREDICTIONS FROM INSIDERS AFTER GOP LOSSES, BUT TRUMP ISN'T BUDGING YET

"With @StephenM taking on this new role for President Trump, I’ve decided to stop recording new podcast episodes," Katie said in a post on X. 

"Nothing is more important than raising our four kids. While I’ve loved the podcast, the time commitment is too great and now is the time to step away. I’ll be cheering President Trump and his team on from outside the administration," she added.

Katie said the podcast will release two more episodes that were recorded before her decision.

Trump named Miller as his new chief of staff Friday, calling him one of his "most trusted advisors." 

A White House official told Fox News Digital the decision was also "very amicable" and Wiles handed in her resignation Thursday night.

item.title: After GOP's brutal midterms, ‘Chuck Norris of Florida politics’ tells party to 'get up and fight'
item.description: Republican Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins, dubbed the "Chuck Norris of Florida politics" by Ron DeSantis, says the GOP must rise like warriors.
item.content:encoded:
When an insurgent's bullet shattered his arm in combat, Republican Florida Lt. Gov. Jay Collins did not wait around for an evacuation team; the Green Beret performed emergency surgery on himself to save the limb.

After the midterms that Gov. Ron DeSantis called a "near extinction-level" event for Republicans, Collins sees a national GOP lying bloodied on the field. He advises his battered and beaten party to show the same refusal to die, and get up like a warrior.

"Where we go from here is up to us as a Republican Party," Collins, dubbed the "Chuck Norris of Florida politics" by DeSantis, told Fox News Digital in an interview just days after the midterm "bloodbath."

"This can be a definitive death blow if we allow it to be, but I believe in what we stand for." he continued. "I believe in our Constitution. I believe in our founding fathers' vision. I believe that God blessed this nation. I think we have to knuckle down, learn, apply this, and we have come out with a relentless dedication and fury to focus on what matters: To lead our state, to lead our country, and be what we need to be for the American people. That is what we should choose to do."

"Hard times happen. Warriors, leaders get up and fight. That's what we have to do now."

DESANTIS CALLS GOP MIDTERM LOSSES 'EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' — AND EXPLAINS WHY FLORIDA SURVIVED

The metaphor is not subtle. It is a road map, set forth by DeSantis' two four-year terms – the last year of which was supplemented by Collins as his No. 2.

HUGH HEWITT: THE GOP IS WOUNDED, NOT DEAD — BUT RECOVERY HAS TO START NOW

Collins said his home state's recent history of going from a purple state to a GOP stronghold is an example the rest of the country can follow.

"Florida's been the road map," he said. "I think we've been what I call the conservative proving grounds. I think that it's time for many here in Florida to use our voice and to be out there and help our party get back on their feet. Be resilient. Yeah, man, you got popped. You got hurt. Get back up, dust it off, and let's go lead. Let's learn."

While congressional Republicans scramble to assign blame for a devastating cycle of national losses – including the loss of Texas to Democrats – Florida has positioned itself as the country’s preeminent conservative fortress, now the largest red state on the 2028 map.

"Losing sucks, winning is awesome: Let's get back to more winning," he said. "We've just got to figure out how we're going to do that, and that's achievable. I think Florida is a blueprint. I think we have a responsibility to lead."

DAVID MARCUS: HOW ASHLEY MOODY SURVIVED THE BLUE TSUNAMI AND EMERGED AS A GOP STAR

Under DeSantis, Florida shed its long-held "purple" swing-state identity to become the nation's largest, most disciplined red bastion. Collins looked back on how he pulled in the no party affiliated voters (NPAs), the valued middle that can flip races and states, in his state Senate race before being tapped to serve under DeSantis.

"Republicans showed up, but the NPAs showed up and they overwhelmingly did not align with Republicans," Collins said, admitting that even Florida's heavy Republican registered voter edge led to slim margins in the tough midterm environment. "What does that tell us? Well, the biggest gap we had was that we didn't spend enough time communicating to our NPAs."

Collins pointed back to how he won a Tampa race in a district "that is not a conservative juggernaut in terms of Florida," running against the Tampa mayor's mother-in-law.

"This was my very first race," he recalled. "We didn't talk to a single Republican out there. We only knocked NPA's and light D's, and we won by 10. What does that tell you? In a community like Tampa, I didn't hide from my views. I told people I'm conservative, I'm a Republican."

JASON CHAFFETZ: FIVE TIMELESS POLITICAL LESSONS THAT GOT LOST IN 2026

"What I realized is if you're honest with people, you agree on more than you don't, but you have got to be willing to step in there and have that conversation," he said. "And we did that over and over and again. And we built a base of people who trust us, because I don't play games."

"As a party, we need to go back to being the party that welcomes folks in – a little bit more of a big tent – but we have to stand on our conservative values," he added.

Collins is termed out of office along with DeSantis in January, but he will evaluate his future in the state or the national party apparatus. For now, he is committing to nothing and merely saying, "Stay tuned."

TREY GOWDY: THE MIDTERMS WERE A PAINFUL LESSON THAT REPUBLICANS CAN'T SKIP LEARNING

Regardless of candidate or party, Collins goes back to his military background and having risked his life and literally sacrificed limb for unity.

"I wore a flag on my shoulder every single day that I served in uniform," he said. "I wore the flag on my suit, really every single day that I was out there, serving in our state or serving our nation in any way that I could. We're the American people; we are blessed."

Once the party picks its 2028 candidate, Republicans need to be all-in against the opposition, Collins said.

"We have to row the boat," he said. "Sept. 11 was a big day in our life. Sept. 12 was incredible because we saw the power and the might of what America can be. When we rowed the boat, our enemy was fearful. They were on their heels because they saw an absolute juggernaut standing righteously to defend our people and our way of life. What our enemy fears, what other nations fear is Americans coming together."

TRUMP-BACKED BYRON DONALDS TO MAKE HISTORY AS FLORIDA’S FIRST BLACK GOVERNOR

"We have to come together and realize that our nation is blessed," he continued. "It will fall if we don't come together. But it won't happen if we don't start uniting and remind ourselves that this is America, we're allies, internal in our country, and we're going to make sure that it's the greatest country moving forward. America's worth fighting for."

"We need to focus on getting through this, the aftermath of this cycle, wrap it up, transition, and make sure that we understand exactly what happened," he concluded. "You know, when we started the war on terror, and I was a young soldier, we spent two years trying to fight the last war. It wasn't very great, to be honest with you.

"Let's not fight the last war. Let's understand the operational environment. Let's under our gaps. Our weaknesses and how we can clearly address those. And then we're going to have to move with a righteous fury."

item.title: Patrick Mahomes suffers apparent elbow injury on throwing arm but returns to face the New York Jets
item.description: Patrick Mahomes took a hit to his right elbow while throwing and was left grasping his arm in pain, but stunned fans by returning to face the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Mahomes left the Kansas City Chiefs game against the New York Jets with what appeared to be a serious injury to his right (throwing) arm Sunday afternoon, but that was only because we forgot that this guy is apparently made of rubber.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback took a hit from New York Jets edge rusher David Bailey as he was winding up to throw a deep pass. Instead, his arm hit Bailey as the defender closed in on Mahomes.

The ball fluttered to the ground as an apparent fumble.

PATRICK MAHOMES ANSWERS TROUBLING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS SERIOUS KNEE INJURY ON FIRST DRIVE OF THE CHIEFS SEASON

Mahomes was left on his knees, grasping his right elbow, in obvious pain.

PATRICK MAHOMES SO OBSESSIVE ABOUT KNEE REHAB HE TAKES A TRAINER WITH HIM WHEN HE LEAVES TOWN

The shocking thing of all this? Mahomes returned to the game.

The man is Gumby.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Despite seeming to favor the arm as he tried to make throws on the sideline, Mahomes returned to the game on Kansas City's next series and threw a completion to tight end Travis Kelce.

Then he scrambled up the middle for a 7-yard gain.

This is not normal.

After halftime, which almost definitely included another evaluation of Mahomes' elbow, the quarterback went back into the game. And he helped the Chiefs drive for a touchdown and a 21-12 lead.

After the game, Mahomes said he was scheduled for more testing and admitted that he didn’t feel great but "if I’m able to play, I’m gonna play" going forward. 

Mahomes also said he wasn’t "throwing the ball the way I wanted to" after halftime, but felt better as the game went on.

"From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can’t throw," Mahomes said of the difference between a serious injury and what he has. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn’t — hopefully, I haven’t done the test yet, it wasn’t ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff. That’ll be important to kinda get worked out this week." 

It is clear that Mahomes avoided a UCL tear because such an injury to his elbow would prevent him from throwing the football. San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy suffered such an injury in the playoffs several years ago.

item.title: George W Bush welcomes 27 veterans to his ranch for 16th annual Warrior Ride

item.content:encoded:
Former President George W. Bush welcomed 27 veterans to his ranch in Crawford, Texas, for his 16th annual Warrior Ride, an event honoring their service and recovery ahead of Veterans Day.

"These veterans have overcome a lot... but there's no self-pity. There's no, 'Please feel sorry for me,'" the 43rd president said on Friday.

item.title: Social media horrified by Dave Chappelle’s sick ‘joke’ about Charlie Kirk’s murder
item.description: Circulating video from Dave Chappelle's Madison Square Garden show captures him saying he does "feel better" after the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Dave Chappelle said he feels "better" following the assassination of Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk during a stand-up performance in New York City on Friday night, provoking outrage across social media.

Despite rules barring cell phones from the Madison Square Garden show, a video circulating on social media shows Chappelle appearing to make the remarks during his "Karmageddon" tour stop in New York City.

"I feel f----- up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy, Charlie Kirk, got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but, I feel better."

'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL

"I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling. I didn’t ask to feel this way," Chappelle said. He then described his unexpected high spirits in the aftermath of Kirk's killing.

"I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!'" Chapelle continued on Friday.

TPUSA pointed Fox News Digital to Erika Kirk's statement on X, in which she wrote that treating the destruction of human life as a punchline is "disgusting."

"A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard," she continued.

"Shame, shame, shame on Chappelle," Elon Musk posted.

Benny Johnson, host of "The Benny Show" podcast, called Chappelle's remarks "sick," while political commentator Meghan McCain asked, "What the h--- is wrong with Dave Chappelle?!"

Former communications director to former Vice President Mike Pence Katie Miller tagged Live Nation, the entertainment behemoth that sold tickets for Chapelle's tour, on X and asked, "Is this something we agree with?"

Journalist Piers Morgan wrote that Chappelle's comments were "especially egregious given that Chappelle himself survived an attack on stage in 2022." 

Many on X pointed out that Charlie Kirk himself posted in support of Chappelle after the comedian was attacked. Kirk wrote that refusing to charge the comedian's assailant sent "a clear message that public acts of political violence are justifiable." The man who attacked Chappelle was ultimately charged with four misdemeanors.

Kirk was murdered at a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University in Orem on September 10, 2025.

A trial date for Tyler Robinson, 23, the alleged shooter, has not yet been set.

PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST

Robinson has pleaded ⁠not guilty to all seven charges filed against him. His attorneys are seeking to block cameras from an upcoming hearing.

Chappelle has received backlash for his edgier jokes over the years, including jokes about transgender people. 

Pushback against part of his stand-up show "The Closer," released on Netflix in 2021, led to a small group of Netflix employees staging a walkout in protest. 

Kirk's murder has been the subject of multiple comedians' sets, including, Pete Davidson, who faced backlash after an explicit joke during Netflix’s "The Roast of Kevin Hart" at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. 

"Tony reminds me of Charlie Kirk in that he’s definitely been on camera letting a guy unload in his throat," Davidson said during the roast. 

"Saturday Night Live" "Weekend Update" co-anchor Michael Che also joked about Kirk's killing during his Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota."

"I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way," Che said. 

Che said he didn't know who Charlie Kirk was before the activist was killed, joking that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek."

Fox News Digital reached out to Chapelle's team and Madison Square Garden for comment but did not immediately hear back.

item.title: Forget prunes: Popular green fruit shows promise for constipation relief
item.description: A review of 33 studies links eating two green kiwis daily for four weeks to more regular bowel movements in people with constipation or IBS-C.
item.content:encoded:
Eating two green kiwis a day could help people struggling with constipation, a new review suggests.

The research, published in the journal Food, Nutrition and Health, looked at 33 previous studies and reports on kiwifruit and digestive health.

Eating two fresh green kiwis a day for about four weeks was linked to more regular bowel movements, less straining and better digestive comfort in people with constipation or irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C).

COMMON KITCHEN STAPLE MAY HELP RELIEVE MILD CONSTIPATION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

In one international trial included in the review, people with constipation had about 1.5 more complete bowel movements per week, while those with IBS-C had about 1.7 more per week. Both groups also reported improved digestive comfort.

The new review suggests there may be several reasons kiwi helps with constipation.

Its fiber can add bulk and hold water in stool, while the fruit's natural water and sorbitol may help make stool easier to pass. Researchers said the benefit likely comes from several parts of the whole fruit working together rather than one component alone.

Kiwi was not necessarily more effective than other constipation treatments.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

One U.S. trial included in the review found that green kiwi, psyllium fiber and prunes all helped improve chronic constipation. Kiwi was associated with fewer side effects and was well-tolerated by many participants.

The evidence is strongest for fresh green kiwi, the researchers noted. There is less research on gold kiwi, powders and extracts, so those forms should not be assumed to have the same effect.

Jason Heiselman, a New York-based certified nutritionist and professional chef at Hungryroot in New York City, previously told Fox News Digital that kiwi is an easy fruit to work into a person's diet.

"It feels like a no-brainer to include a few slices with any meal," said Heiselman, who was not involved in the new review.

For people who do not want to eat kiwi on its own, the fruit can also work in savory meals, according to Heiselman. "Raw kiwi slices often make their way to my dinner table," he said.

Heiselman said he pairs the fruit with salty cheeses, toasted pistachios and shaved red onion, and has also used kiwi as the base for chutneys and relishes.

There were some limitations to the findings.

The paper reviewed previous research rather than conducting a new clinical trial, and the studies differed in the people involved, the types and amounts of kiwi consumed, and the results researchers measured.

Most of the research also looked at relatively short periods of time, so more studies are needed to determine whether the benefits continue long-term.
